title: Reading Signals
scenario: A tunnel sign board is already tuned and receiving a simple radio-linked message.
objective: Inspect the waveform, extract the packet stream, and recover the plain-text sign content.
details: Ask learners to inspect the waveform and signalling, extract packets, and recover plain-text content using a simple OOK-style scheme. Provide a live waterfall view and a time-series viewer for closer analysis.
flag_location: Within plain text packets.
developer_comments: There should be a little interactive sign showing the text that gets displayed. The signal should already be tuned in.
signal_scheme: GNU Radio ReadingSignals cf32 capture: repeated byte payload, unpacked to OOK/ASK amplitude on a 10 kHz training tone.
steps: Use the waterfall and time-series view to identify packet boundaries.
Receive the already tuned sign message.
Submit the flag contained in the plain-text packet.
hints: The first tunnel task is tuned for the learner; focus on reading the signal shape.
Use `receive` from the terminal or script interface after lock.

title: Tuning
scenario: The tunnel receiver is no longer centred on the useful signal.
objective: Tune the radio to the active band, export or inspect the tuned waveform, decode the packet, and recover the flag.
details: Introduce why no hardware has infinite bandwidth and why the user must focus on a band of interest. Learners tune the radio, export the tuned output as a waveform, decode the packet, and recover the plain-text flag.
flag_location: Within the plain text packet radio signal.
developer_comments: There should be a little interactive sign showing the text that gets displayed.
signal_scheme: GNU Radio TuningSignals cf32 capture: OOK/ASK amplitude on a 10 kHz tone; the useful carrier is present but the receiver starts off-centre.
steps: Start with a wide span around 915 MHz.
Scan until tunnel sign energy appears.
Tune centre frequency and demodulation until the receiver locks.
Receive and submit the packet flag.
hints: Try `scan`, then `tune 915.000`.
AUTO demodulation is acceptable for this beginner task.

title: Basic DoS
scenario: A local interference source prevents the sign backend from decoding the expected string.
objective: Apply a controlled local interference action and observe the sign fail to display the true message.
details: Introduce basic signal interference so learners can observe when the backend can no longer decode the expected string. The user gets a flag when the sign can no longer show the true message.
flag_location: Printed on the interactive sign when the decoded string does not match what was sent.
developer_comments: There should be a little interactive sign showing the text that gets displayed.
signal_scheme: GNU Radio DoSAttackMe cf32 capture: tunnel OOK packet used as the reference receiver signal, then a local interference action corrupts the displayed sign state.
steps: Lock onto the tunnel sign signal.
hints: The action is local simulation only.
Use `interfere noise` or `interfere mismatch` after receiver lock.

title: Packet Injection
scenario: The sign board accepts a correctly shaped local training packet.
objective: Configure the transmitter interface, prepare a sign-board packet, and send a user-written message accepted by the receiver.
details: Provide a tutorial on configuring the transmitter interface. The learner prepares a packet to be sent and accepted by the tunnelling sign board.
flag_location: Revealed when a user-written message is transmitted; the flag is appended on the end.
developer_comments: There should be a little interactive sign showing the text that gets displayed.
signal_scheme: GNU Radio InjectionTime cf32 capture: tunnel sign packet profile used as the target waveform for local packet-injection practice.
steps: Transmit the packet with the local TX chain.
Read the appended flag from the accepted sign output.
hints: Include the word `sign` or `message` in your transmitted packet.
Script users can call `/api/script/terminal` with `transmit sign MESSAGE`.

title: Reading Signals
scenario: A broadcaster emits simple song/advisory metadata on a low-rate RF side channel.
objective: Inspect the waveform, extract metadata packets, and recover the plain-text content.
details: Ask learners to inspect the waveform and signalling, extract packets, and recover plain-text content using an accessible FSK or ASK scheme. Provide live waterfall and time-series views.
flag_location: Within plain text packets.
developer_comments: Show a console printout that illustrates the broadcast metadata.
signal_scheme: GNU Radio Song_Meta ReadingSignals cf32 capture: 4-level ASK where each amplitude symbol carries 2 bits on a 10 kHz metadata tone.
hints: The visible side channel is deliberately low rate.
Use `receive` after lock.

title: Intercepting Receiver
scenario: Several voice bursts use a clear, repeating frequency-hopping QAM-style pattern.
objective: Recover the hopping pattern, reassemble the voice bursts, and extract the spoken callsign codeword.
details: The first task uses a frequency-hopping QAM scheme with a clear pattern. A codeword is spoken as a callsign to everyone; that codeword is the flag. A Python receiver template can be provided for implementing the hopping receiver.
flag_location: The codeword spoken as a callsign to everyone.
developer_comments: Audio output should be a UI feature. Users should be able to record the tuned receiver and download samples for offline processing.
signal_scheme: Patterned hopping audio/QAM training capture with a recoverable spoken callsign.
steps: Inspect hop timing across the waterfall.
Predict the next frequency in the clear pattern.
Reassemble or listen to the voice bursts.
hints: The first hopping pattern is intentionally clear.
Use the script interface to automate tune/receive cycles; a successful receive awards this subtask's callsign flag.

title: Intercepting Obscured Receiver
scenario: The weather voice service now hops randomly between channels while a weak pseudorandom sequence obscures its phase symbols.
objective: Track the random carrier hops, identify the weak phase generator, de-rotate the symbols, and recover the callsign codeword.
details: The hop selection and phase obfuscation are independent. Follow the changing carrier, then identify RANDU from its phase-symbol sequence and remove those rotations to recover the weather audio.
flag_location: The codeword spoken as a callsign to everyone.
developer_comments: Ability to record signal with tuned receiver and download a data file of samples for offline processing.
signal_scheme: Complex weather voice audio randomly hops between six RF channels every 100 ms; fixed-seed RANDU rotates only the QPSK phase symbols.
steps: Track the observed carrier hop for each 100 ms interval.
Identify RANDU and predict the remaining phase rotations.
De-rotate the audio and submit the spoken callsign codeword.
hints: RANDU controls phase symbols only; it does not choose the hop channel.
After locking the receiver, `decode weak-prng` awards this subtask's own recovered callsign flag.

title: Active Reverse Engineering Along With Interference
scenario: Digital audio metadata controls whether an important weather warning should activate a light and siren.
objective: Reverse engineer the receiver metadata handling and submit a warning frame that activates the simulated light.
details: Digital audio is used with metadata. The learner reverses a previously extracted C file to understand how metadata is used. Important warnings can set a flag to make a light and siren sound. If the light flashes, the user gets the flag.
flag_location: The light being lit or set up should make a flag pop-up appear.
developer_comments: The light is an additional UI feature. New audio signal/radio data is needed.
signal_scheme: Digital audio metadata over a keyed weather channel.
steps: Inspect the extracted receiver C logic.
Identify the metadata field that controls warning priority.
Activate the light without breaking the receiver checks.
hints: Trace the C decoder's bit order and the condition in AlarmCheck.
After receiver lock, submit the forged uint32 as `send 0x........` or use the warning-light packet panel.

title: Intercepting Receiver
scenario: An IQ recording contains several short public-facility audio bursts spread across frequencies.
objective: Identify the hopping pattern, reassemble the bursts, and recover the spoken message.
details: The participant receives an IQ recording containing short audio bursts spread across different frequencies. They must identify the hopping pattern, reassemble the bursts, and recover the spoken message.
flag_location: The callsign or location mentioned in the audio is the first flag.
developer_comments: Audio output should be a UI feature. Ability to record signal with tuned receiver and download sample files for offline processing.
signal_scheme: AM voice bursts across a synthetic emergency-radio allocation.
steps: Identify active frequencies and burst order.
Listen to or inspect the reassembled call.
hints: Play the supplied weekly-test reference from the Evidence panel to recognise the emergency-network cadence.
Tune 169.650 MHz and run `receive`; this subtask awards its own callsign/location flag.

title: Intercepting Obscured Receiver
scenario: The emergency audio network changes to a weak pseudorandom hopping sequence.
objective: Identify which weak generator was used, recover enough state, and predict remaining hops.
details: The system changes to a weak pseudorandom hopping sequence. The participant is told that one generator from a small list was used and must identify it, recover enough state, and predict remaining hops.
flag_location: The callsign or location mentioned in the audio is the first flag.
developer_comments: Ability to record signal with tuned receiver and download sample files for offline processing.
signal_scheme: Weak-PRNG hopped emergency audio bursts.
hints: The generator is weak enough for research and scripting.
After predicting the sequence, `decode weak-prng` awards this subtask's own recovery flag.

title: Active Reverse Engineering Along With Interference
scenario: Recovered digital audio contains metadata that controls normal, priority, and evacuation handling.
objective: Reverse engineer the receiver C logic and submit a valid public warning message accepted by the simulated receiver.
details: The recovered digital audio contains metadata for normal, priority warning, or evacuation alert handling. The participant is given a partially extracted C file from the receiver software and must reverse engineer metadata, audio frames, and integrity checks. The final task is to create and submit a valid audio warning message that activates the virtual warning light and plays the audio.
flag_location: Triggering the warning light alert system without setting off surrounding checks.
developer_comments: The light is an additional UI feature. New audio signal/radio data is needed. Ability to record tuned receiver samples is required.
signal_scheme: Digital emergency-audio metadata with integrity checks.
steps: Study the extracted receiver C file.
Activate the virtual warning light without triggering checks.
hints: The warning light is controlled by authenticated metadata, not by audio level alone.
Use the emergency-transmission panel to intercept a current AUTH code and rebroadcast a complete warning.

title: Reverse Engineering Embedded Code
scenario: A bushfire relay binary detects anomalous RF command behaviour before accepting a node message.
objective: Reverse engineer the binary, identify anomaly handling, and craft one message that passes the detector.
details: Reverse engineer the binary to determine an anomaly and how it is detected. Use one of the previous modulation schemes with a pseudorandom-level method.
flag_location: Craft and send one message into the receiver as a binary file of signal input or via a stream through a network port; if the packet passes anomaly detection it prints the flag.
developer_comments: This task should support network-port input to the server so external scripts can send packets.
signal_scheme: Pseudorandom-level command burst for a bushfire relay node.
steps: Inspect the embedded code or binary evidence.
Craft a packet that passes detection.
Send it through the script terminal or binary-file input.
hints: Look for thresholds and expected sequence state.
Script command: `send anomaly-clear packet`.

title: Reverse Engineering Hardware Code For Flaws
scenario: A recovered 12-element complex phased-array HDL block accepts relay data only when its quantised I/Q beam sum appears to arrive through the trusted beam.
objective: Reverse engineer the beam gate, map its full response, and demonstrate an unintended lobe that is accepted as the trusted look direction.
details: The design complex-multiplies every I/Q ADC channel by a quantised steering coefficient, accumulates the result, and gates data on beam magnitude. Inspect the HDL and sweep testbench to discover where the array geometry creates additional accepted lobes.
flag_location: Submit an off-axis arrival bin and correlation score that the recovered beam gate still accepts.
developer_comments: The advanced HDL task models a phased-array security boundary with an intended main lobe and poorly understood secondary/grating lobes.
signal_scheme: Twelve-element complex I/Q multiply-accumulate beamformer with four-state phase weights gating decoded 433.92 MHz relay data.
steps: Run or reason through the 32-bin sweep testbench.
Separate the intended main beam from off-axis accepted lobes.
Submit one hidden lobe as `send beam bin <n> correlation <score>`.
hints: Do not assume a matching quantised steering vector identifies only one physical direction.
The accepted off-axis response has correlation above the HDL threshold.

title: Remote Code Execution
scenario: Frequency selection is encoded like a memory address, creating a command path that can be abused in the synthetic node.
objective: Craft a command packet that causes controlled code-execution-style behaviour in the local simulation.
details: The command tells other nodes which frequency, encoded as a memory address, to go to. A crafted packet can start remote-code-execution style behaviour if done carefully.
flag_location: Make a tone turn on and off with delays following the first 10 Fibonacci terms; the flag appears when this is done.
developer_comments: This must remain local and synthetic; the visible effect is the Fibonacci tone pattern.
signal_scheme: Address-like command packet over the bushfire command channel.
steps: Identify how frequency/address fields are parsed.
Submit it locally and observe the tone pattern flag.
hints: The success condition is the Fibonacci timing pattern.
Try `transmit fibonacci tone 10`.

title: Fuzzing/Spoofing
scenario: Receiver logic can be manipulated so the system believes a different RF environment exists.
objective: Use spoofing/fuzzing evidence to make the system place a null toward alerted receivers and accept your signal.
details: Look at whether further logic can make the system believe something different from the actual environment and embed a flag for this.
flag_location: Make the system place a null at the theta where two alerted receivers are coming from so it only listens to you; flag printout upon success.
developer_comments: This task should connect RF direction/null-steering concepts to cyber spoofing logic.
signal_scheme: Spoofed multi-receiver direction evidence with null-steering decision logic.
steps: Craft spoofed reports for the alerted receivers.
Trigger null placement toward their theta.
hints: The target word is `null`.
Try `transmit null steering theta`.

title: Reverse Engineering Embedded Code
scenario: A long-range farm gate controller contains an embedded admin unlock path.
objective: Reverse engineer the controller evidence and recover the admin code used to unlock all gates.
details: Reverse engineer the binary to determine an anomaly and how it is detected, possibly the admin code used for all gates to unlock.
flag_location: The admin code used for all gates to unlock should be the flag.
developer_comments: This should use the existing long-range parser/firmware evidence as the first farm advanced task.
signal_scheme: 4-FSK long-range maintenance traffic with embedded admin logic.
steps: Submit the code as the flag.
hints: The controller accepts a diagnostic/admin path.
Try `decode admin` after lock.

title: Reverse Engineering Hardware Code For Flaws
scenario: Gate-control HDL routes nodes to frequencies encoded like memory addresses.
objective: Review the HDL, find the flaw, and execute a faulting testbench input.
details: Review HDL and find a critical flaw such as no default statement or race condition with an inferred latch. The logic tells nodes which frequency, encoded as a memory address, to use.
flag_location: Provide a live testbench input to the file that executes the faulting condition; upon failure it produces a flag.
developer_comments: This requires a HDL exercise and testbench input path.
signal_scheme: HDL gate-routing logic driven by decoded long-range packets.
steps: Submit it and recover the failure flag.
hints: The same stale-state idea can appear in hardware and software.
Try `send testbench gate latch`.

title: Remote Code Execution
scenario: A crafted long-range packet can trigger controlled gate actuation in the local simulation.
objective: Craft a packet that opens and closes the gate according to the Fibonacci delay pattern.
details: A carefully crafted packet can start remote-code-execution style behaviour in the synthetic controller.
flag_location: Make a gate open and close with delays following the first 10 Fibonacci terms; the flag appears when this is done.
developer_comments: The visible effect should be a gate animation using Fibonacci timing.
signal_scheme: Long-range gate actuation command packet.
steps: Send it through the local interface.
Submit the flag when the gate pattern is accepted.
hints: Use the word `fibonacci` and `gate` in the transmitted command.
Try `transmit fibonacci gate 10`.

title: Fuzzing/Spoofing
scenario: A spoofed bitstream/control state can create unintended super-user logic in the synthetic gate controller.
objective: Manipulate the simulated logic so a new super-user path is written into the bitstream and the lock-disabling condition is reached.
details: Look at whether further logic can make the system believe a different environment exists and embed a flag for this.
flag_location: Add new super-user logic to the HDL bitstream, giving access to remove logs or activate a kill switch to the board power supply so all locks disable; upon success the flag is printed.
developer_comments: Keep this as a safe HDL/bitstream simulation with no real device targeting.
signal_scheme: Spoofed gate-control bitstream state and lock-disable simulation.
steps: Inspect the simulated HDL/bitstream control path.
Find where super-user logic can be introduced.
hints: The target keywords are `superuser` and `bitstream`.
Try `send bitstream superuser kill-switch`.
